findings.reason: the write paths must gain these two test files (rewriting the cases §27 supersedes, as §26 did for the analogous case), otherwise the section's mechanism and its done-when are mutually unsatisfiable and the node stalls at the regression clause.
findings.text: §27 changes `_cached_run_time_profile` to never rebuild (serve last persisted when the stamp moved and it is younger than 24h, else serve none), moving the rebuild to a promotion-triggered refresh; but two live test files whose entire premise is the removed behaviour are absent from §27's write paths — `tests/test_picker_foreign_wait_is_bounded.py` (`test_a_moved_ledger_is_read_against` asserts a moved stamp forces a fresh `run_time_profile` read, line 127; `test_two_picks_read_each_foreign_ledger_once` asserts the foreign ledgers are read and the wait is 420.0, line 83; `test_a_fresh_process_with_no_records_reads_no_ledger`, line 294) and `tests/test_dispatch_speed.py` (`test_profile_reuses_marker_published_during_initial_read` asserts `calls == ["sample"]` after two calls, line 698; `test_profile_does_not_cache_across_a_source_change` asserts `count` 1/2/2, line 763) — so the done-when's "no added failure" clause cannot hold within the granted scope and the node would fail its own gate or be forced to write fenced files

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited symbol resolves: `run_time_profile`, `_cached_run_time_profile`, `_expected_wait`, `local_lane` (reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py), `capabilities.cached_pick_input_rekeyed`, `capabilities._read_pick_entry`, `capabilities.pick_input_cache_path` (reckon/capabilities.py), `reckon/crew/promotion.py`, `reckon/crew/picker/prompts.py`, the emitted string `timeout in pick:state-render` (reckon/crew/dispatch_picker.py:542, tests/test_a_pick_names_its_slow_stage.py:328), and the cited figures (6,555 / 1,254 / 99.5% / 41.0% / 164 / 15.31%) match the research doc's own tables.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the done-when's regression clause ("the test files importing `lane_context.py` or `promotion.py` show no added failure against the base revision") is unachievable within §27's declared write paths, because two live test files exercise the rebuild-on-miss behaviour §27 removes.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — cited evidence is the research doc `docs/research/the-pick-state-render-is-slow-because.html` and the node's tests under `tests/`; no scratchpad or node-local path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `persisted_at` and `expected_wait_profile_age_s` carry no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag; plan labels appear only in plan HTML, which is permitted.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the cited evidence (the research doc's cause section names exactly `_cached_run_time_profile`'s synchronous rebuild. The mechanism runs on the real path with callers named (`_expected_wait`, and promotion on the ledger append), and the age-disclosure field follows the doc's "serve a bounded last-good snapshot with its age disclosed". The regression clause defect belongs to the done-when item below, not to the mechanism.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §27's deliverable is one capability (a pick never rebuilds a profile), and `expected_wait_profile_age_s` is the age disclosure the same capability requires, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §27's `depends-on` (`lane-and-model-routing#s25`, `jev-learns-from-its-routes#s5`) resolves: §25 is done, jev §5 exists (the one-staleness-rule section, which writes `lane_context.py`/`prompts.py`) and has landed on main; the interleaving across both plans (jev §6 runs after §27) is acyclic.
